correctness.rationale: The repaired claim uses the already-established all-q finite-dimensional gap only as input. For a fixed q, normalize a subsequence so Gaussian cotype and the (q,1)-summing norm are at most one while Rademacher cotype grows at least \(4^k\). Weighting the block maps by \(2^{-k}\) on the c0-direct sum gives an operator-norm limit of finite-rank block truncations, hence a compact operator. The \(q\)-power sum bounds give finite Gaussian cotype and finite (q,1)-summing norm, while tests supported on one block force the Rademacher cotype constant to exceed \(2^k\) for every k. Each finite block embeds isometrically into an l_infinity block, so the c0-sum domain is a closed subspace of c0.
